newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks drift off, ignore Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks drift off, ignore Wall Street.

text.p: Mexican stocks shunned Wall Street bulls to extend their early slide in light midsession trade on Wednesday due to lack of foreign investor interest and poor corporate earnings, traders said.
"The market is very slack. Foreigners who are still here are very selective, but I think most are in New York and Brazil," a desk trader.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 13.92 points, or 0.37 percent, at 3,743.34.
Trading volume .TV.MX was dull at 47.2 million shares.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones was meanwhile up 67.83 points to 7,029.46. In Brazil, the Bovespa .BVSP index was up 121 points to 9,979.
"It is company earnings that are holding us down. Investors don't want to step in," a floor trader said.
Nonetheless, traders said share prices could recover towards the close on month-end buying for portfolio valuation purposes.
"We know things could pick up, even if only in the last five minutes. They'll prop it up in a little while," a trader said.
